AUDIT-C Alcohol Use Screening — FHIR Questionnaire Template

Three-question alcohol consumption screen with an automatic total score (0–12) and the usual positive-screen thresholds.

Open in Builder

Scoring

Each answer scores 0–4. The total (0–12) is a positive screen at 4 or more for men and 3 or more for women.

Questions

  1. How often do you have a drink containing alcohol?
    • Never
    • Monthly or less
    • 2-4 times a month
    • 2-3 times a week
    • 4 or more times a week
  2. How many standard drinks containing alcohol do you have on a typical day?
    • 1 or 2
    • 3 or 4
    • 5 or 6
    • 7 to 9
    • 10 or more
  3. How often do you have 6 or more drinks on 1 occasion?
    • Never
    • Less than monthly
    • Monthly
    • Weekly
    • Daily or almost daily

Calculated results

  • AUDIT-C total score (0–12)

Source and license

Source: Bush et al. 1998, Arch Intern Med 158:1789 (AUDIT-C, from the WHO AUDIT). Codes and answer lists: LOINC, as in the HL7 US Core AUDIT-C questionnaire. (link)

License: No restrictions on use (per the ONC USCDI/ISP listing; submitted by NIAAA). (link)

Provided to save authoring effort, not as medical advice — confirm the scale and its cut-offs for your use case.

Use it

  1. Download the FHIR Questionnaire JSON, or
  2. open it in the Builder right away (or open the Builder, choose + Add → From template… and search for “AUDIT-C Alcohol Use Screening”). It arrives as one titled group with its calculations wired, and you can keep editing it.
